classification.difficultyReason: Link the taught multiplicity rules, interval signs and leading-term behaviour to construct sign diagrams and sketches, distinguishing flattened crossings from touches.

content.prompt: Identify the zeros of each polynomial. Draw sign diagrams and sketch the curves.

answer.short:
Zeros: $x=-4,4$ (both double).

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&x<-4&-4&-4<x<4&4&x>4\\\hline\text{Sign of }y&+&0&+&0&+\end{array}$

The curve touches the axis at both zeros; both ends rise. The $y$-intercept is $256$.
answer.worked:
Setting each factor equal to zero gives $x=4$ or $x=-4$. Both factors are squared, so the polynomial is positive except at its zeros.

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&x<-4&-4&-4<x<4&4&x>4\\\hline\text{Sign of }y&+&0&+&0&+\end{array}$

$y(0)=(-4)^2(4)^2=256$.

Both zeros have even multiplicity, so the curve touches the $x$-axis at each. Its leading term is $x^4$, so both ends rise.

spec.description: Equation-driven sketch with double zeros at -4 and 4 and y-intercept 256; no numerical vertical scale implied.

answer.short:
Zeros: $x=-1,4$ (both triple).

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&x<-1&-1&-1<x<4&4&x>4\\\hline\text{Sign of }y&+&0&-&0&+\end{array}$

The curve crosses with flattening at both zeros; both ends rise. The $y$-intercept is $-64$.
answer.worked:
The factors give zeros $x=4$ and $x=-1$, each of multiplicity $3$. For $x<-1$, both cubed factors are negative; between the zeros their signs differ; for $x>4$, both are positive.

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&x<-1&-1&-1<x<4&4&x>4\\\hline\text{Sign of }y&+&0&-&0&+\end{array}$

$y(0)=(-4)^3(1)^3=-64$.

The sign changes at each triple zero, so the curve crosses and is flat near each zero. Its leading term is $x^6$, so both ends rise.

spec.description: Equation-driven sketch crossing flatly at -1 and 4, with y-intercept -64 and both tails rising.

answer.short:
Zeros: $x=0$ (triple), $x=4$ (multiplicity $4$).

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&x<0&0&0<x<4&4&x>4\\\hline\text{Sign of }y&-&0&+&0&+\end{array}$

The curve crosses flatly at $0$ and touches at $4$. Its left end falls and its right end rises.
answer.worked:
The factors give $x=0$ with multiplicity $3$ and $x=4$ with multiplicity $4$. Away from $4$, $(x-4)^4$ is positive, so the sign is determined by $x^3$.

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&x<0&0&0<x<4&4&x>4\\\hline\text{Sign of }y&-&0&+&0&+\end{array}$

The sign changes at $0$, giving a flattened crossing. It does not change at $4$, giving a flattened touch. The $y$-intercept is $0$. The leading term is $x^7$, so the left end falls and the right end rises.

spec.description: Equation-driven sketch with flattened crossing at zero, local positive hump and fourth-order contact at four.

answer.short:
Zeros: $x=-2,0$ (both multiplicity $4$).

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&x<-2&-2&-2<x<0&0&x>0\\\hline\text{Sign of }y&+&0&+&0&+\end{array}$

The curve touches flatly at both zeros; both ends rise.
answer.worked:
The factors give zeros $x=0$ and $x=-2$, each of multiplicity $4$. Both fourth powers are positive away from their zeros, so their product is positive there.

$\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&x<-2&-2&-2<x<0&0&x>0\\\hline\text{Sign of }y&+&0&+&0&+\end{array}$

There is no sign change at either zero, so the graph touches the axis and is flat near both. The $y$-intercept is $0$. The leading term is $x^8$, so both ends rise.

spec.description: Equation-driven nonnegative sketch with fourth-order contacts at -2 and zero and a positive hump between them.
